asr.full_text: Just one result could change the course of their lives. Pull, pull, pull, pull, pull, keep going, keep going. This is RBC Training Ground, a nationwide event that puts athletes like Sydney Wilkins to the test in the search for Canada's next great Olympians. I've always been interested in the Olympics. I feel like it's an awesome way to get introduced to that world. First up, the speed test. Speed, what are we looking for? Looking for. This one's a lot of fun. The athletes ability to go from zero. Standing start to full velocity in a shorter period of time as possible. FYI speed is something Olympic cyclist Kurt Innes knows a thing or two about. It. Comes down to two types of muscle fibers slow twitch and fast twitch. The slow. Ones help with endurance activities while the fast twitch muscles allow us. To spring to action. This one most definitely talking fast twitch fibers. Of the athletes with a higher percentage of. It's trainable, yes, but those of us that have that innate ability to turn on right away. So that's Usain Bolt's secret. Okay, and he did train very, very hard. Pull, pull, pull, pull, pull. Next, strength. Simultaneously pull the chain while pushing off the floor as hard as you can. It is way harder than it looks. So they're starting from a very fixed position. It's all about timing. So how do they turn and turn off different muscles? Here we go. I found that one actually surprisingly difficult. Told ya. But hey, if that's your jam, you may have what it takes to be a rower taking those first few powerful strokes. A sprint cyclist starting from standing where they have to get that big fixed gear going. Or a freestyle skier using all their strength to manage forces when landing. Moving on to the vertical jump. Watch out LeBron James. So the athlete must be able to get down into an explosive position and then use that counter. Movement to really try to jump up as high as they can. And then just that physical ability to be able to recruit that fast twitch muscle fibers. That they have. In rugby, this skill comes in handy when hoisting a player in a line out, or in speed skating. When the athlete explodes from the start line. Last, endurance athletes' fave, run to the line before the beep. Just to mess you up, keep speeding up. So their heart rates are going to elevate for sure,. Respiration rates are going to increase,. Blood pressure as well. It's going to feel terrible. So they have to actually physically try their best. To calm themselves down, keep breathing. Remember slow twitch muscles? Athletes with more of those will be able. To endure this longer and may have a future. In speed skating, canoe kayak, and rowing. Pretty tough. I found it really encouraging though,. Being with everyone, being in the gym,. Everyone was like, gee. Sydney is hoping that boost made the difference. To get an invitation to the next round of tests. And the RBC Training Ground National Final,. Where eventually the top athletes will get support. For training to pursue their podium dreams.
